item.title: 36.16 - MU Podcast - Beneath the Pyramids
item.description:

Welcome to your Plus+ Extension, and thank you all for joining us on Plus+! item.title: 36.15 - MU Podcast - This Hollow Earth - Episode 06: The Coming Race and Vril Power
item.description:
Welcome to Mysterious Universe Season 36, episode number 15! If you are not already on Plus+, your FOMO must be a-flutter, because this is episode 06 of our This Hollow Earth Saga. Sign up in the link below to catch up on this incredible journey.
Today, on episode 06, we get to one of the most important discussions of the hollow earth’s actuality, found within the pages of the novel, THE COMING RACE AND VRIL POWER by Edward Bulwer Lytton. This is the so-called “fictional story” that inspired one of the most sacred beliefs of the Third Reich and ushered in an ambitious and bizarre point of interest for these well-dressed delinquents.
Then for Plus+, we ask what if the Great Pyramids of Egypt were built to preserve an entire civilization rather than bury its kings? Exploring Scott Creighton's The Secret Chamber of Osiris, we follow his investigation into ancient flood legends, the sixteen pyramids, and a mysterious location beyond the Giza plateau where he believes a hidden chamber may still exist. From disputed hieroglyphics and forgotten engineering techniques to an unexpected excavation in the desert, it's a wild journey into one of Egypt's enduring mysteries.

item.title: 36.14 - MU Podcast - The Tayos Caves Mystery Part 1
item.description:
Welcome back to MU! Deep beneath the Ecuadorian jungle, explorer Juan Moricz claimed to have discovered an enormous cave system containing strange architecture, golden artifacts, and a library of ancient knowledge written on thousands of metal plates. From conflicting eyewitness accounts and Father Crespi’s bizarre collection to Erich von Däniken and a massive 1976 expedition involving Neil Armstrong, we follow the Tayos mystery as one extraordinary claim turns into a decades-long obsession nobody has been able to completely settle.
And for your Plus+ extension we enter Episode 05 of our Hollow Earth Saga as we get down to why the underground is so freakin’ cool with legends of treasure vaults and subterranean tunnels that permeate this porous earth. Starting out with a Llama meeting real-life Agarthians with two tongues, then we head on over to South America in search of underground treasure vaults and secret tunnels. We have seen evidence for the holes in the poles. We have spoken with the Llamas in Tibet about the King of the World that resides and reigns in the inner earth. We have traveled the Orient with Adventure Hound Doc Anderson and been given more questions to ask...And now, we go deeper…

item.title: 36.12 - MU Podcast - The Skill Trap | Outsourcing Ourselves
item.description:
Welcome back to MU! As AI and automation get better & better at doing our jobs, they may also be slowly doing away with the way humans have always learned to become good at them. With examples from robotic surgery, Michelin kitchens, warehouses, bomb disposal, banking, and more, our second installment of Matt Beane’s The Skill Code explores how we build real expertise, and how intelligent machines could either hollow that process out or help create an entirely new kind of apprenticeship. 
Welcome to your Plus+ extension, and thank you all for joining us on Plus+! Buddhists believe that millions of super cool people reside in this underworld paradise called Agartha. Their daily lives and their destiny are directed by a wise, all-powerful ruler known as Rigden-jyepo, also known as the King of the World. Rigden-jyepo kicks it in Shamballah, the capital city of Agartha, which is allegedly accessed through many secret entrances from the surface world, found hidden within the towering monasteries of Tibet, guarded by jolly llamas sworn to protect the secrets of the underworld.

item.title: 36.11 - MU Podcast - This Hollow Earth - Episode 01: Deep Lore
item.description:
Welcome to Mysterious Universe Season 36, episode 11! According to Buddhist doctrine, Agartha is a subterranean land located deep within the center of our planet. Buddhists believe millions of people live in this underground paradise. Their lives and destinies are directed by an all-powerful and all-wise ruler. What wonders lie just beneath us all? We are here today to begin a fascinating saga series titled This Hollow Earth, based on the work of Warren Smith in his 1977 book, This Hollow Earth - The astounding investigation into the 'lost worlds' beneath our planet’s surface.
We are here to ask: is the story of Agharta nothing more than a fun fable, or is there truth behind the legend? Do we know the Earth is solid, with varying layers of deep, dense material that terminates in a solid molten core? Or could there be vast inhabitable spaces we would be astounded to experience?

item.title: 36.08 - MU Podcast - Free-Running | The Human Clock
item.description:
Welcome back to MU! This week we take a look at Why Time Flies by Alan Burdick and find out that even “official” time is a negotiated average built from clocks around the world. Then we move into the story of Michel Siffre, who removed himself from daylight, clocks, calendars, and ordinary human routine, and his cave experiments reveal just how quickly the body's internal rhythms can drift when they're cut loose from the outside world.
Welcome to your Plus+ Extension, and thank you all for joining us on Plus+! Animals, along with all living things, are affected by cosmic rhythms and celestial cycles. Snails and crabs live by the tides, even in laboratories nowhere near the ocean. Cats with internal clocks that can be adjusted on command. Disappearing dogs that return without fail every Christmas. Biological clocks are nature's timing systems here to help regulate the behavior of all forms of life. From the simplest organism to man himself, and do so quite efficiently. Today we enjoy the 1970 book The Strange World of Animals and Pets by Vincent and Margaret Gaddis. Dedicated to all the pets, who rule us with an iron paw.

item.title: 35.22 - MU Podcast - UFO Reflections | Abductions
item.description:
UFOs capture our attention like nothing else can as we hear stories of these flying wonders and contemplate their origins, missions, and purposes. Some captivate more than others, literally capturing unsuspecting citizens to be brought aboard these enigmas for more baffling experiences. Philip Mantle is an outstanding researcher, author, and firsthand witness to the world of the freaky woo-woo.His new book, “UFO Reflections,” boasts a wide variety of said “woo” and offers us all greater insights into this highly strange phenomenon.
In our Plus+ extension, we visit an MIT computer scientist and game designer Rizwan Virk in his book The Simulation Hypothesis as he takes a swing at one of the wildest ideas floating around modern culture: what if reality itself is basically a massively multiplayer simulation? He tries to connect ancient mystical ideas with modern computational thinking. Whether he’s onto something profound or just brilliantly overthinking Zelda, this one opens up a ton of questions about consciousness, perception, and what this place actually is.
